data.name: Yolantia
data.gender_notes: Yolantia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman name Iolanda, Yolantia means 'jolly' or 'delightful' in Latin. It is often associated with the warrior saint Yolanda of Hungary, who is remembered for her kindness and bravery. The name Yolantia carries the meaning “Jolly warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Yolantia usually hope their child will grow to embody jolly warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Yolantia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jolly warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yolantia total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: יולנטיה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא האור שלי, שושנת השדה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יולנטיה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו ביוונית ופירושו 'אלוהים הוא האור שלי' או 'שושנת השדה'. השם נגזר מהמילים היווניות 'ιός' (yol) שפירושה 'אלוהים' ו-'λάνθη' (lanthe) שפירושה 'אור'. השם יולנטיה מופיע בתקופה של ימי הביניים וקשור אל קדושים נוצרים.

in_greek.name: Ιολάνθεια
in_greek.meaning: Θεός είναι το φως μου, το κρίνος του πεδίου
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Ιολάνθεια είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέχεται από την ελληνική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Θεός είναι το φως μου' ή 'το κρίνος του πεδίου'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'ιός' (yol) που σημαίνει 'Θεός' και 'λάνθη' (lanthe) που σημαίνει 'αφθονία' ή 'φως'. Η Ιολάνθεια ήταν γνωστή κατά την περίοδο του Μεσαίωνα και συνδέεται με χριστιανική παράδοση.

in_latin.name: Yolantia
in_latin.meaning: Deus est lux mea, lilium agri
in_latin.long_meaning: Yolantia est nomen christianum quod originem in lingua graeca habet et significat 'Deus est lux mea' vel 'lilium agri'. Nomen derivatum est ex vocibus graecis 'ιός' (yol) quod significat 'Deus' et 'λάνθη' (lanthe) quod significat 'lux' vel 'abundantia'. Yolantia in medio aevo nota erat et ad traditionem christianam pertinet.

in_english.name: Yolantia
in_english.meaning: God is my light, Lily of the field
in_english.long_meaning: Yolantia is a Christian name derived from Greek roots, meaning 'God is my light' or 'Lily of the field'. It originates from the Greek words 'ιός' (yol), meaning 'God', and 'λάνθη' (lanthe), meaning 'light' or 'abundance'. The name Yolantia emerged during the Middle Ages and is associated with Christian tradition, symbolizing spiritual illumination and purity. It reflects a connection to divine guidance and natural beauty.

data.cultural_impact: The name Yolantia has connections to various European cultures beyond its Latin origins. In Hungarian folklore, Saint Yolanda of Podók, also known as Yolanda of Humilium or Yolanda of Palermo, is venerated as a patron saint of travelers, students, and the blind. Her life story and legacy have influenced the use of the name Yolantia in other parts of Europe, particularly in the Iberian Peninsula where it became popular among Christians during the Middle Ages.
data.spiritual_significance: Devotion to Saint Yolanda, alongside her jovial meaning, adds a deep spiritual significance to the name Yolantia. She is revered for her excellent learning, devotedly studying the scriptures in secret when her parents tried to keep her from accessing education. Yolantia's name transcends its dictionary definition and carries the spirit of joy and wisdom. It is a reminder that learning and knowledge bring happiness and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yolantia: God's Grace and Strength in Sorrow. A name for those who find solace in the Lord during times of grief and suffering. The 'Yo' represents the Lord's presence, while 'lantia' symbolizes the strength and grace bestowed upon the bearer in their time of need.

historical_references.reference: Yolanthe of Aragon (1154-1211) was a queen consort of Aragon, Navarre, and Sicily. She was the eldest daughter of Alfonso II of Aragon and Sibylla of Barcelona. Yolanthe played a significant role in the Crusades, particularly the Second Crusade, where she accompanied her husband, King Alfonso II of Aragon, to the Holy Land.

Saint Yolanda of Ferrara (1212-1258) was an Italian Blessed of the Catholic Church, also known as Blessed Yolanda of the Rogation. She was born into a noble family in Ferrara, Italy, and was known for her piety and charitable works. She founded the Order of the Holy Savior, a religious community dedicated to the care of the sick, and is venerated as a patron saint of the sick and those suffering from incurable diseases.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Yolantia, of Latin origin meaning 'wide land', is popularly used in various modern contexts, particularly in the realms of mythology, fantasy literature, and role-playing games. On platforms such as Reddit, users may discuss the character Yolantia, a goddess from Slavic mythology, or create role-playing characters with this name in mythology-based communities. Goodreads users may add books with the title 'Yolantia' to their virtual shelves, often fantasy novels with that name. In tabletop RPG communities, players may choose the name Yolantia for their game characters, further expanding the use of this name beyond its historical origins.
